c1.text: Gather round. I've got a scary story.

c2.text: It's about a kid, his snooze button, and an alarm clock that came back from the dead.

s1.text: Dylan was always late for school.

s2.text: Not because he overslept. Because he snoozed. Professionally.

s3.text: One day he cleaned his room, which is honestly the scariest part of this story.

s4.text: He tripped over the cord, the alarm clock went dark,

s5.text: and he plugged it back in like nothing happened.

s6.text: It blinked back to life. But it wasn't the same clock.

s7.text: The next morning it went off, and his hand stopped halfway to snooze.

s8.text: Is that the real time? How long was it dead?

s10.text: He had no idea. So he got up.

s11.text: He was on time for days.

s12.text: Then he worked out the offset, fixed the clock, and was late again by Monday.

r1.text: Dylan grew up, but he never forgot that clock.

r2.text: In 2012 he built it as an iPhone app that looked like a slot machine.

r3.text: He tried to buy LotteryClock.com. The owner said no.

r4.text: The app never shipped. The idea died.

r5.text: But some things don't stay dead.

r6.text: This Kiroween, Dylan dug it back up.

h2.text: Pick when you want to wake up.

h3.text: Then drag the dial to pick how much you're willing to gamble:

h4.text: five minutes, ten, or forty-five if you're truly unwell.

h5.text: LotteryClock hides the real alarm somewhere in that window.

h6.text: Could be early. Could be late. You don't get to know.

h7.text: Rings early? You win. Snooze guilt-free until your target time.

h8.text: Rings late? You lose. Get up. You're already late.

h9.text: And because you can't tell which one it is, you get up anyway.

h11.text: Once your clock can't be trusted, your brain can't snooze on autopilot.

t1.text: Every theme has its own way of telling you you're late.

t2.text: Good Night. It counts sheep while it decides your fate.

t3.text: Día de Muertos. Win, and you rest in peace.

t4.text: Lose, and you rise from the dead. Which is basically every Monday.

t5.text: Ouija. Let the spirits pick. The spirits say: rise.

t6.text: Tarot. Push your luck and the card catches fire.

t7.text: Upright, you sleep. Reversed, you're up.

t8.text: And for the high rollers: a prize wheel and a poker table.

t9.text: Two ways to go bust before breakfast.

a2.text: The website is the game. The iPhone app is the real thing.

a4.text: But tap Set Alarm, and it schedules a real alarm with Apple's AlarmKit,

a5.text: at a random moment inside your window.

a6.text: The phone knows when. You don't.

a7.text: When it rings, the alarm tells you how it went.

a8.text: Rang early? Hit snooze, and you get exactly the minutes you won,

a9.text: then it rings again at your target time.

a10.text: Rang late? No snooze. Up you get.

a11.text: Open the app and the clock rolls to reveal when it really went off.

a12.text: Every morning lands in your history,

a13.text: so you can see exactly how many minutes of sleep you've gambled away.
